newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fighting in northwest Colombia leaves 18 dead.
newsitem.headline: Fighting in northwest Colombia leaves 18 dead.

text.p: Eighteen people, including 10 soldiers, were killed in combat early on Saturday in the notoriously violent region of Uraba near Colombia's northwest border with Panama, authorities said.

Spokesmen for the 17th Army Brigade said the fighting erupted at dawn in four municipalities of Uraba, a banana-growing region where gunmen of the left and right have been battling for control over lucrative drug and contraband smuggling routes for years.
In addition to the 10 soldiers gunned down by rebels, eight Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas were killed, the spokesmen said.

They said FARC fighters, who senior military officials recently claimed had retreated from Uraba in the face of a massive counterinsurgency sweep of the region, had blown up a bridge outside of the small town of Piedras Blancas before disappearing into the surrounding countryside.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla force, launched a dramatic, nationwide offensive in late August in which scores of police and soliders were killed and hundreds wounded.
